tools.name: connect
tools.description:
Connect from the named project profile only.

        Probe, target, and external board-config overrides are intentionally absent. For a
        deliberate exceptional manual connection, initialize connect_override-plan instead.

tools.name: disconnect
tools.description: Close the named board session and release only its connection.

tools.name: get_board_info
tools.description: Return active profile and routing facts for the named board.

tools.name: get_state
tools.description: Return the connected core's current observable run state.

tools.name: halt
tools.description: Halt the selected board's core.

tools.name: resume
tools.description: Resume the selected board's core.

tools.name: step
tools.description: Single-step and return the resulting program counter.

tools.name: reset_and_run
tools.description: Reset and execute from the reset vector without changing target security.

tools.name: read_cpu_register
tools.description: Read one runtime-supported ordinary CPU or floating-point register.

tools.name: read_execution_state
tools.description: Read one runtime-supported control-flow or execution-state register.

tools.name: find_symbol
tools.description: Search the current firmware ELF for a bounded list of matching symbols.

tools.name: read_memory_symbol
tools.description: Resolve and read a mapped, non-prohibited symbol; prefer it to raw access.

tools.name: remove_breakpoint
tools.description: Remove one breakpoint at an exact hexadecimal or decimal address.

tools.name: wait
tools.description: Pause for 1-60000 milliseconds for one logical board workflow.

tools.name: connect_override-plan
tools.description: Connect using explicitly reviewed exceptional identifiers without changing profiles. Use only after normal connect or validation resolution fails and you can state the exact failure. It is for exceptional manual probe unique_id, pyOCD target, logical board definition, or external board configuration. Never use it to conceal a hardware/profile mismatch the user should correct. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan supports a bounded multi-call budget. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: reset_and_halt-plan
tools.description: Reset the selected board and halt immediately at startup. Use when firmware fails immediately and startup state must be inspected. reset_and_run is always available and needs no plan for an ordinary restart. This action is not an unlock and never changes target security. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan supports a bounded multi-call budget. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: connect_under_reset-plan
tools.description: Attach while physical reset is asserted, then halt and release reset. Use after normal attach fails because firmware sleeps, reconfigures debug pins/clocks, or crashes too early. It asserts physical reset, attaches over SWD, halts, and releases reset. It is not an unlock; a protected target still requires target_unlock. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan supports a bounded multi-call budget. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: write_cpu_register-plan
tools.description: Write an ordinary general-purpose or floating-point CPU register. Use while halted to patch an ordinary R0-R12 or supported floating-point register. Read it first with read_cpu_register. Do not use this for PC, SP/MSP/PSP, LR, xPSR, CONTROL, PRIMASK, BASEPRI, FAULTMASK, or security/provisioning registers; use set_execution_state for supported execution-state registers. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan fixed to one call with budget 1,0. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: set_execution_state-plan
tools.description: Change a CPU control-flow or execution-mode register. Use only for a deliberate write to PC, SP/MSP/PSP, LR, xPSR, CONTROL, PRIMASK, BASEPRI, FAULTMASK, or a related supported execution-state register. reset_and_run is always available and safer for restarting; use write_cpu_register for ordinary data registers. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan fixed to one call with budget 1,0. The populated plan requires legitimate one-time or full-session user permission. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: register_write-plan
tools.description: Apply one masked value to a documented peripheral register. Use for one documented peripheral/configuration register read-modify-write. The complete word must be in a mapped peripheral window. Flash security, option bytes, OTP, debug protection, provisioning, and lifecycle registers are unavailable—no plan can authorize them, and calling an address a register does not make it one. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan fixed to one call with budget 1,0. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: read_memory_address-plan
tools.description: Read a mapped address or bounded memory block when symbol access is unsuitable. Prefer symbol access whenever source code or debug symbols identify the intended variable (find_symbol and read_memory_symbol are always available and need no plan). Use raw addresses only for dynamically allocated, pointer-derived, stack, optimized-out, or otherwise unsymbolized memory. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan supports a bounded multi-call budget. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: write_memory-plan
tools.description: Write one symbol-backed value or an explicitly justified mapped RAM address. Use to change one variable for a bounded hypothesis test. Prefer a symbol. A raw address requires allow_address_fallback=true plus a concrete reason and is RAM-only. Do not use this for peripheral registers or flash. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan fixed to one call with budget 1,0. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: set_breakpoint-plan
tools.description: Set a breakpoint at one mapped executable symbol or address. Breakpoint-and-step debugging is escalation, not the first move. First use tagged UART print instrumentation and read_serial to reconstruct flow. Use a breakpoint only when prints failed or cannot work—for example before UART initialization, timing perturbation, no UART path, or instruction-level inspection after logs localized the fault. remove_breakpoint is always available and needs no plan. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan fixed to one call with budget 1,0. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: flash_application-plan
tools.description: Flash a validated artifact wholly inside the application partition. Use only to deploy a rebuilt application artifact. Never use it for a bootloader or arbitrary flash. The server checks every loadable segment, required erase sector, entry point, vector table, target identity, and artifact-defined load addresses against the application partition. The request never supplies a target address. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan fixed to one call with budget 1,0. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: flash_bootloader-plan
tools.description: Flash a validated artifact wholly inside the bootloader partition. Use only for an artifact intended for the bootloader partition. Application, prohibited, ROM-bootloader, and unknown regions are rejected. Prefer flash_application for ordinary firmware changes. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan fixed to one call with budget 1,0. The populated plan requires legitimate one-time or full-session user permission. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: read_serial-plan
tools.description: Capture bounded UART output from the selected board. Use for bounded UART boot text, logs, or injected diagnostic prints. It is not a continuous monitor; each capture is bounded by read_seconds. expected_text=null is the right choice for exploratory captures so one exact plan can cover varied output. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan supports a bounded multi-call budget. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. tools.name: write_serial-plan
tools.description: Send bounded UTF-8 text over the selected board's UART. Use to send bounded UTF-8 input to a firmware CLI or test menu. The exact text is frozen; a different command requires a replacement plan. Pair it with planned read_serial observation. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan supports a bounded multi-call budget. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: serial_exchange-plan
tools.description: Run a bounded multi-step UART conversation through one state-preserving port open. Use after firmware is safely flashed for one or more ordered console commands whose responses or volatile state must survive between commands. Prefer this over separate write_serial/read_serial or repeated serial_exchange calls: those require separate port opens, and some USB-UART bridges reset firmware on open. All steps are validated before the server opens the port, then run in order on that one handle. Complete setup routing and board_validate before using this hardware plan. First call this tool with every parameter NULL; its response explains the mechanism, exact nested action_parameters JSON, warnings, soft checks, permission, and next call. This plan supports a bounded multi-call budget. No user permission grant is required, but the plan is still mandatory. Submit only the exact plan JSON returned by that flow; prose and extra fields are rejected. After acceptance, prefer the exposed direct action. If client bindings stay static, use only the exact server-returned one-child action_batch fallback unchanged.

tools.name: setup_overview
tools.description:
Inventory profiles/connections and route user-provided familiar board names.

        Call after initialization_handshake and after asking which boards are connected. Pass the
        ordinary familiar names here; pass NULL only to inspect inventory before the user answers.
        The normalized literal sentinel "no board" must be passed by itself and is never a board
        name candidate. If it is mixed with names, re-ask the user conversationally.
        Every matching stored name, including an incomplete profile, routes to board_validate
        first. Unknown names receive a server-generated board_id plus setup questions. Use setup,
        repair, safety, attachment, or retry only when validation names that exact remedy. Relay
        only agent_prompt and friendly choices, never raw identifiers or this JSON.

tools.name: load_setup_tool
tools.description:
Load detailed setup/validation guidance for one server-generated board_id.

        Call setup_overview first so the server, rather than the user, supplies the profile route,
        board_id, and friendly physical choices. Then load exactly the setup tool named by that
        route before calling it. Never ask the user for board_id, connection IDs, or JSON.

tools.name: board_setup-plan
tools.description:
Run this setup-routing plan first before any other *-plan hardware tool.

        Use the all-NULL call before attempting hardware access. It explains how to ask for the
        board's familiar name and exact board/MCU identity, route an existing matching YAML profile
        to board_validate, and load the hidden setup workflow only when the profile is absent or
        validation fails. Do not populate a setup plan for a healthy profile that validates.

tools.name: continue_setup
tools.description:
Continue an incomplete setup with one server-requested choice or research reply.

        Call this only when board_setup or board_fix_setup returns setup_needs_user_input or
        setup_research_required. Relay the server's friendly question to the user when required,
        or perform the requested official-source research, then submit exactly the response
        object described by accepted_response/exact_response_fields. This tool validates and
        stages evidence but grants no permission, opens no gate, and performs no target write.
        After acceptance, call board_fix_setup under the still-active paired setup allowance.

tools.name: board_safety_setup
tools.description:
Create the first authoritative safety map, or rebuild one after structural failure.

        Trigger this when board setup/validation reports that no safety map exists, authoritative
        sources are incomplete, regions conflict, or an anchor change requires a full rebuild. It
        is not the routine source-drift path and never opens the hardware gate by itself; call
        board_validate after it succeeds.

tools.name: board_safety_refresh
tools.description:
Refresh an existing valid safety map after safely scoped source or build drift.

        Trigger this only when a current map already exists and validation or a guarded action names
        refreshable fingerprint drift as the remedy, such as a rebuilt application or a rebuilt
        bootloader already contained by a reviewed bootloader partition. Use board_safety_setup for
        a missing/conflicting map and full setup plus validation for board, MCU, target, geometry,
        or schema-anchor changes. Refresh never creates authority and never reopens a disconnected gate.

tools.name: board_validate
tools.description:
Validate a matching board YAML first, or validate after setup, repair, or reconnect.

        Trigger this instead of board_setup when the user's familiar board name already matches a
        healthy profile. A passing validation stamps only the current board/connection gate. If it
        fails because setup or safety evidence is incomplete, follow its exact setup or safety
        remedy; never treat the profile's presence alone as permission to access hardware.

tools.name: get_setup_status
tools.description:
Report whether durable setup and this run's live validated session are ready.

        Call this as the final barrier before an external coding workflow begins. It never opens
        a connection or gate and never treats persisted reports as authority. UART readiness is
        reported separately so a project that does not need a console is not blocked, while a
        console-dependent workflow can require ready_for_uart_work before it starts. For a known
        reviewed MCU, build_guidance returns the exact Zephyr board target and recommends the
        cross-platform pyocd-zephyr-build helper, which uses short scratch paths when necessary on
        Windows. That guidance is advisory only: inspect the resulting ELF/map with
        board_safety_refresh before flashing.

tools.name: target_unlock-plan
tools.description:
Prepare destructive recovery only after setup/validation reports a locked target.

        First call every parameter NULL for the full mechanism and research guidance. Then submit
        one exact JSON plan with user_permission NULL to receive the live identity, complete erase
        ranges/losses, and plan_id disclosure. Relay it plainly, obtain fresh one-time approval,
        and resubmit the otherwise unchanged JSON with user_permission='one-time'. Full-session or
        prior permission never applies; any target, probe, map, range, or plan change invalidates it.

tools.name: action_batch
tools.description:
Execute bounded same-board child calls through their normal dispatch path.

        Use an accepted *-plan's server-generated one-child fallback unchanged when a client's
        callable bindings remain static. Never invent hidden children or use a batch to bypass
        plans, permission, validation, gates, freshness, timeouts, budgets, locks, or cleanup;
        every child independently traverses those normal checks.

BatchChild.description: One JSON-only MCP child call with no extra or authority-bearing fields.
